subject: Post-call scouting: BrightMart model-fit paths and perf links
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@brightmart.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call scouting: BrightMart model-fit paths and perf links

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and pragmatic next steps based on what we heard: BrightMart wants an agent-style assistant for order troubleshooting + product guidance, heavy on short-context Q&A and 3–4 turn conversations, with occasional 1k+ token docs for recall. Primary constraints: predictable latency for UI (p95 target < 250ms) and cost sensitivity at scale.

What we recommend exploring first (scouting evaluation playlist):
- Fast, low-cost baseline: mistral-7b-q4 (good for short-response throughput)
- Higher-quality, instruction-tuned option: semantic-xl-1.3 (better instruction-following on multi-turn)
- Long-context fallback for doc-heavy sessions: llama-2-13b-q4f16 with prefix cache enabled

Redwood-verified perf (representative numbers on our Dedicated A100-40GB profiles; seq len / batch noted):
- mistral-7b-q4 (seq 128 / batch 16): throughput ~2300 tokens/sec; p50 9ms; p95 45ms; p99 90ms
- semantic-xl-1.3 (seq 256 / batch 8): throughput ~850 tokens/sec; p50 22ms; p95 140ms; p99 320ms
- llama-2-13b-q4f16 (seq 256 / batch 8): throughput ~980 tokens/sec; p50 16ms; p95 85ms; p99 160ms

Notes / caveats:
- Benchmarks above assume continuous batching and KV cache hits where applicable; expect higher latencies for cold-start or non-batched single requests.
- We saw occasional quality regressions on semantic-xl-1.3 for long, instruction-heavy prompts that require strict instruction-following; we'll include a prompt-resilience test set to quantify that.

Attached: brief prompt set we used in the call, a CSV with the raw throughput/latency snapshots, and a short PDF with the Redwood model profiles. Also linking the model catalog and the bench gist below.

Proposed next steps (suggested timeline):
1) You share 5 representative flows (we can use the prompt pack attached) — BrightMart ops (by EOD Thu)
2) Redwood runs a 2-day pilot against the three models above with your flows, returns TPS/latency + quality delta report (end of next week)
3) Sync call to review results and pick a pilot model (30 minutes)

If that sounds good I’ll kick off the pilot and send a short scope/MA POC statement for signatures.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: brightmart_prompt_set_v1.txt (text), scouting_benchmarks.csv (csv), redwood_performance_profiles.pdf (pdf)

- For the p95 target we care most about cold-starts under low concurrency (our UI often fires single requests). Do your p95 numbers include single-request profiles?
- On quality: any quick examples of the regressions you mentioned for semantic-xl-1.3? We want to understand risk before the pilot.

I'll pull together 5 flows (order-status check, partial refund flow, product mismatch triage, guided upsell prompt, and a large-doc search query) and aim to share by Thu.

—Lena

Head of AI Product, BrightMart

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@brightmart.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call scouting: BrightMart model-fit paths and perf links

Lena — thanks, and great question on cold-starts. Short answers:

- The attached CSV includes both single-request (no batching) profiles and continuous throughput snapshots. For single-request cold-starts on mistral-7b-q4 we see p95 in the 60–120ms range (seq 128); semantic-xl-1.3 cold single-request p95 is nearer 260–380ms depending on prompt length. These reconcile with the p95s I gave which were blending steady-state and realistic single-request tails; we'll separate them in the pilot report.

- Example of the semantic-xl-1.3 regression: when prompts included multi-step constraints ("only return SKUs available in aisle X and include price band"), we observed hallucinated SKU entries ~6% of the time on a 400-example prompt set vs. <1% for the 7B baseline. The regression looks tied to instruction collapse on long, interleaved constraints — we recommend adding instruction-specific prompt templates and evaluation thresholds.

What Redwood will deliver for the pilot:
- 48-hour bench run per model with separate single-request and steady-state traces
- A prompt-resilience report (precision/recall style checks where applicable) focusing on your five flows
- A TPS/latency heatmap and a latency-percentiles summary per model (p50/p95/p99) with sequence-length breakdowns

I’ve attached the prompt pack and raw snapshots. Links: model profiles and bench gist are in the email metadata.

Can you confirm the flows will include at least one long-doc retrieval example so we can validate prefix cache effectiveness? If yes, we’ll enable cache-on for that test and include the delta.

Thanks — I’ll start scheduling infra for the runs once you confirm.

Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
